claim: Best months Apr-Jun and Jul-Sep; NE monsoon mid-Oct to end Feb closes dive centres and most businesses, ferries curtailed.
quote: The monsoon runs from mid-October through end of February... most tourist activity comes to a standstill from October to March... dive centers close, and visibility becomes too poor for diving.

claim: Best diving months are April-June with peak visibility; dry-season visibility 15-25 m.
quote: the best three months for diving in the Perhentian Islands are typically April, May, and June, when the weather is calm and visibility is at its peak.

claim: Perhentians famous for cheap easy diving for all levels; best season Mar-Oct, viz up to 20m, water ~30C; Batu Nisan good for snorkellers; Tokong Laut signature pinnacle.
quote: easy diving suitable for all levels that is cheap... Best time to visit March to October... visibility typically reaching up to 20 meters... Batu Nisan... can just as easily be snorkelled and still see just as much.

claim: In June 2026 1 EUR is roughly RM4.6 (1 MYR around 0.217 EUR).
quote: As of June 9, 2026, 1 Malaysian Ringgit equals 0.212886 EUR, or conversely, 1 EUR is equal to 4.6109 MYR.

claim: Marine park conservation charge: foreigners RM30/adult, RM15/child; Malaysians RM5/RM2.
quote: Foreign Visitors (Non-MYKAD Holders): Adults: RM 30.00... Children (6-12 years) and seniors (60+): RM 15.00... Malaysian Citizens... Adults: RM 5.00.

claim: Conservation fee is paid at the jetty when visiting the Perhentian marine park.
quote: RM30.00 per adult and RM15.00 per child for the conservation fee.

claim: Shark Point at southern tip of Perhentian Besar near Flora Bay; blacktip reef sharks, hawksbill turtles, reef to 9m; reachable by boat tour (~$25) or 400-500m swim from Flora Bay.
quote: Shark Point sits at the southern tip of Perhentian Besar Island... near Flora Bay... blacktip reef sharks... hawksbill sea turtles... Maximum depth reaches 30 feet... Self-guided swimming from Flora Bay beach—requires 400-500 meter round-trip.

claim: Several reefs snorkelable from shore: Shark Point swim from Flora Bay, D'Lagoon, Long Beach/PIR jetties, Teluk KK/Fish Point.
quote: the best thing about snorkeling in Perhentian is that there are places right on the beach full of life and corals... D'Lagoon... a beautiful reef full of life just a few meters from the shore.

claim: Shark Point yields multiple 2m blacktip sharks; Seabelle Rock lighthouse site has currents; Romantic Beach good snorkel off right-side rocks; tours stop at Fisherman's Village for lunch.
quote: I saw around five sharks in total, measuring up to two metres... Seabelle Rock Lighthouse... stronger currents require caution... Romantic Beach... Best snorkeling near right-side rocks.

claim: Tours visit 5-6 spots incl Turtle Point/Shark Point; kayak from beaches; sunset at Coral Bay and Teluk Keke, sunrise Long Beach; Turtle Beach is the turtle sanctuary.
quote: tours visit 5-6 different snorkelling spots... Sunset: Coral Bay (Kecil) and Teluk Keke (Besar)... Turtle Beach on Perhentian Besar hosts the island turtle sanctuary.

claim: Five-spot day trip from Kuala Besut (Shark Point, Fish Point, Coral Garden, Turtle Point, Fisherman Village) 8am-4pm, RM130 adult/RM90 child incl return ferry and gear.
quote: Shark Point, Fish Point, Coral Garden, Turtle Point, Fisherman Village... Adult: RM130 and Child: RM90... 2 ways boat tickets... FREE Rental of Snorkelling Equipment.

claim: Mat & Man local full-day snorkel trip RM150/pax, 6 stops (Turtle Beach, Turtle Point, Shark Point, Fishing Village, Lighthouse, Romantic/KK Beach), beginner guidance, life jackets.
quote: RM150 per person... Turtle Beach, Turtle Point, Shark Point, Fisherman Village... Nemo Point/Lighthouse, Romantic Beach/KK Beach... Basic snorkeling guidance for beginners.

claim: Snorkel gear RM20/day, guided half-day RM30-40; kayak RM60-80; water taxi RM15-25; turtle watching at Turtle Beach Jun-Sep.
quote: Gear rental: 20 MYR per day... Guided half-day tours: around 30-40 MYR per person... Sea Kayaking: 60-80 MYR for a rental... Water Taxis: around 15-25 MYR.

claim: Sea Voice rates: Discover Scuba RM250, Open Water RM1380, Advanced RM1280, fun dives RM85-110; eco snorkel RM80; night +RM30, T3/Sugar Wreck +RM20.
quote: Discover Scuba Diving: RM 250... PADI Open Water: RM1,380... PADI Advanced Open Water: RM1,280... Fun Dives... RM 110/dive... Eco Snorkeling Tour: RM80/pax... Night dives: RM 30/dive surcharge.

claim: Matahari Divers: Discover Scuba RM250 (~2.5-3h), Open Water RM1350 (3-4 days, free DAN insurance), Advanced RM1250.
quote: Discover Scuba Dive (DSD): RM250... PADI Open Water Course: RM1,350... Includes free DAN Insurance... PADI Advanced Open Water (AOW): RM1,250.

claim: Dive site catalogue: Tokong Laut/Temple of the Sea (18m, advanced), Sugar Wreck (18m), Vietnamese Wreck (24m, advanced, currents), T3, Sail Rock, Shark Point, Batu Nisan, with species per site.
quote: Tukun Laut (Temple of the Sea)... Vietnamese Wreck... Depth: 24m... challenging currents... Shark Point... best place to see blacktip sharks around Perhentian... Batu Nisan... perfect for beginners, checkout dives or courses.

claim: Beginner sites Batu Nisan and D'Lagoon (12m); Temple of the Sea/Tokong Laut 24m pinnacle with whale shark chance; Sugar Wreck advanced-only due to currents.
quote: Batu Nisan (Depth: 12m)... ideal for first dives... Temple of the Sea/Tokong Laut (Depth: 24m)... Huge pinnacle... turtles, trevally, and possibility of whale shark... Sugar Wreck... Strong currents... experienced divers only.

claim: Sugar Wreck is a 90m cargo ship that sank in 2000 during a monsoon, advanced-level, with barracuda, groupers, lionfish, bamboo sharks.
quote: A 90-meter sugar hauler that sank in 2000 during a monsoon... Advanced divers are recommended for this site... several bamboo shark, lion fish, barracuda, puffer-fish.

claim: Flora Bay Divers (Besar) is the first and only PADI 5-Star Instructor Development Centre and dive resort on the Perhentians; runs the Sugar Wreck and Anak Pulau trips.
quote: the first & the only PADI 5 Star Instructor Development Centre and Dive Resort in Perhentian Island, Malaysia... the famous Sugar Wreck, Secret Reef.

claim: Turtle Bay Divers is based on Long Beach, Perhentian Kecil and markets the best-value diving in Southeast Asia; daily PADI courses.
quote: Sunrise on Long Beach, Perhentian Kecil... PADI diving courses... Perhentian offers the best value diving in South East Asia.

claim: Quiver Dive Team is at Coral Bay, Perhentian Kecil, a PADI 5-Star Career Development Centre with 20+ years experience.
quote: Coral Bay, Pulau Perhentian Kecil, 23300, Terengganu... comprehensive PADI certification programs including Open Water, Advanced Open Water.

claim: PADI lists 7 dive centers in the Perhentian Islands.
quote: 7 Dive centers in Perhentian Islands.

claim: Bioluminescent plankton on Perhentian best viewed near Long Beach via night snorkel tour, brightest Apr-Sep on dark calm nights.
quote: Pulau Perhentian (Terengganu): Best viewed near Long Beach... Perhentian Island Night Snorkeling Tour... offers bioluminescence viewing... April-September on the east coast.

claim: The blue-tears bioluminescence phenomenon occurs at Malaysian beaches including Pulau Perhentian, best on dark calm nights.
quote: the blue tears phenomenon occurs naturally at night, contributed by algae or marine plankton that emit blue-green light upon nightfall.

claim: Coral Bay-Long Beach walk 10-15 min easy; Long Beach to windmills ~30 min moderate, sandy/slippery; windmill pier stairs broken and unsafe; good shoes needed.
quote: Coral Bay to Long Beach... 10-15 minutes... not a hike, it is just a walk... windmill trail ascends steeply... The floor is very sandy and slippery... broken stairs leading down to Windmill Pier... not in good shape.

claim: Long Beach to Coral Bay jungle trail is ~700m, 10-15 min, easy and partly paved, no guide needed.
quote: the trek takes 10 to 15 minutes at a leisurely pace... Easy (partially paved)... No guide is necessary.

claim: Windmill (Kincir Angin) viewpoint is a ~20-25 minute hike from Long Beach/Coral Bay with panoramic views.
quote: 20-25 minutes hike from Long Beach / Coral Bay.

claim: Windmill scenic hike ~30 min; Besar trek Turtle Beach to Teluk Keke; Long Beach fire shows ~22:00; Turtle Beach closed after 18:00 to protect nesting.
quote: Windmill Scenic Spot Hike - A 30-minute walk... fire shows around 22:00... Turtle Beach Visit... beach access prohibited after 18:00 for protection.

claim: Long Beach is busiest with nightlife; Coral Bay quieter; Adam & Eve most secluded boat-only romantic beach; Tuna Bay (Besar) good for sunset; Turtle Beach is a nesting beach.
quote: Long Beach (Busy)... Coral Bay Beach (Quieter)... Adam and Eve Beach (Most Secluded)... only accessible by boat... Tuna Bay... excellent for sunset viewing.

claim: Snorkel/dive tours from RM40; cross-island jungle trail on Besar and Long Beach to Turtle Beach on Kecil; kayaking on main beaches.
quote: Organized tours from 40 MYR per person... Cross-island trail on Perhentian Besar... Trail from Long Beach to Turtle Beach on Perhentian Kecil.

claim: Perhentian Besar has a mapped loop hiking trail (Big Loop Island Stop).
quote: Big Loop Island Stop, Trengganu, Malaysia - 57 Reviews, Map | AllTrails.

claim: Bubbles Turtle Conservation runs 5-night programs (ocean/early season Mar-mid Jun; turtle/peak Jun-Oct) RM1350-1800, accessible by speedboat from Besut jetty, open to short-term visitors 18-59.
quote: Ocean & Conservation Experience... Duration: 5 days/nights... Cost: RM1,350-1,750 per person... Turtle Conservation Experience... RM1,400-1,800... accessible by speedboat from Besut Jetty.

claim: Sea turtle protection volunteer programs are offered on the Perhentian Islands for 2026.
quote: Protection Of Sea Turtles | Volunteer in Malaysia 2026.

claim: Perhentian Turtle Project offers education (Know Your Sea Turtles), photo-ID citizen science, and volunteer/intern weeks; turtle hotline +60 19-272 3208.
quote: Send us your turtle photographs from your visit to the Perhentian Islands... Turtle Hotline: +60 19-272 3208... green sea turtles (Endangered) and hawksbill turtles (Critically Endangered).

claim: Day trip from Perhentian to Redang and Lang Tengah: ~09:00-15:00, 5-6 hours, RM150/pax min 2, gear included.
quote: depart from Perhentian at 9:00am, snorkel at 3-4 points on Redang... continue snorkeling on Lang Tengah... RM150 per person with a minimum of 2 people... 5-6 hours.

claim: Three-island snorkel day trip covers Bidong (Kara/Coral Point), Redang Marine Park, Lang Tengah (Blue Coral), 6 snorkel points, from RM180/pax min 8.
quote: visits Bidong Island with snorkeling at Kara Point and Coral Point... Redang Island... Lang Tengah Island... Blue Coral and Batu Bulan... Rates start as low as 180 MYR per person... minimum of 8 adults.

claim: Redang, Lang Tengah and Bidong snorkeling day trip is bookable, including marine park ticket and 6 snorkel points.
quote: Redang, Lang Tengah, and Bidong Islands Snorkeling Experience... includes boat return, snorkeling equipment, marine park ticket, and 6 snorkeling points.

claim: Adam and Eve Beach on northeastern Perhentian Kecil is a secluded romantic boat-only beach with white sand and turquoise water.
quote: the Adam and Eve Beach is a secluded romantic beach that is popular among couples... northeastern tip of Pulau Perhentian Kecil... only accessible by boat.

claim: The islanders' only village, Kampung Pasir Hantu, is at the southeast bulge of Perhentian Kecil.
quote: The sole village of the Perhentian islanders is at the southeast bulge of Perhentian Kecil island.

claim: Highlights include the Pinnacle dive (operators Panorama Diver, Turtle Bay Divers), jumping off the lighthouse, the southern-tip fishing village visit, and Coral Bay as a sunset haven.
quote: climbing and jumping off of a tall lighthouse and into the deep sea below... A small Terengganu fishing village at the southernmost tip of Kecil makes for an interesting afternoon visit... Coral Bay on Kecil... a sunset-watching haven.
